derived.description: CR-04: values fixed once, when character creation completes. The first rule whose condition holds wins, and its values can be written as {name} in any text the narrator sees.
derived.$comment: Settled into the save when creation completes (state.derived); state_store then substitutes {name} into ctx.story, so no prompt builder handles it.

option_count.description: How many numbered options end each scene. The engine asks for exactly this many and parses this many (story_engine, app). Absent means 3; fewer than 2 would not be a choice.

scene_length_by_moment.$comment: CR-14 (Story_Mechanics_Update.md): the scene's word range follows the moment, chosen in code before narration - finale, then a fired pacing directive (or CR-13's push), then the previous turn's beat, then narration.scene_length. inquiry is narrator-judged. Absent means every scene uses scene_length.

beats.description: A range per pacing-loop beat, used for the turn after a scene classified as that beat.

directive.description: When a pacing directive (or the idle-turn push) fires this turn.

finale.description: Every turn once an ending is committed.

inquiry.description: Narrator-judged: when the player's action is only a question or a look around.

oneOf.title: Label only
oneOf.description: A bare label, e.g. "a brass key". Read as an item with that label and nothing else.

condition.$comment: CR-02 (Story_Mechanics_Update.md): the canonical leaf spellings are {"stat": "sync", "gte": 70}, {"revealed": id}, {"relationship": name, "tier_gte": label}. The pre-overhaul gate forms - stat as {axis, at_least}, revelation, character-object relationship - stay accepted: CR-02 rewrites them, no template edits needed.

bond.$comment: CR-11: a directed bond, [from, to], compared with gte/lte/between (score) or tier_gte/tier_lte (mechanics.bonds.tiers labels). A bond that has not opened yet reads as 0. Inside a side-thread recipe's eligible_when, from/to may be the recipe's cast slot names.

on_enter.$comment: CR-01: fires on an upward crossing into this tier. Read by bounded_counter: one directive for the narration after the crossing; `once` limits it to the first entry.

directive.x-visible-when: one turn, on entering the tier

flags.$comment: CR-02: every flag a condition names must be declared here. Not an engine - no `engine` key, nothing to bind; the state-update pass is handed each `detect` so a declared flag can actually be set.

item.title: Item record
item.description: An inventory item as the tagged_items engine keeps it. The engine mints ids for items gained in play; a starting item may author its own.

id.description: What the model cites to spend or lose this item, e.g. itm_001.

label.description: What the item is, as the narrator sees it.

tags.description: Kinds this item counts as, from mechanics.inventory.tags; gates and conditions test these (item_tag).

uses.description: Uses left. With uses, spending one decrements it; without, spending the item removes it.

completion_rewards.$comment: CR-07 (Story_Mechanics_Update.md): the stat events a thread pays when it completes, by the thread's priority (high / medium / low). Each name must be a key of some mechanics.stats.axes.<axis>.costs. A thread's own on_complete.stat_events overrides its priority's row; generated threads inherit by priority.

near_completion_margin.$comment: CR-07: how close to its completion threshold a thread must be for the narrator to be told it may resolve this scene. No engine default: how early to foreshadow a payoff is a creative decision.

transitions.$comment: CR-08 (Story_Mechanics_Update.md): one-shot directives when a relationship's history crosses a line, e.g. once warm and now drifting to neutral, the character exits. Each transition is checked against every relationship after its deltas, once per character unless once_per_character is false.

relationship_when.$comment: The modifiers CR-02's relationship leaf takes, with the character bound by the engine to each relationship in turn (so no name here). All that are present must hold. peak is the highest score the relationship has reached, falling back to its current score.

once_per_character.description: Default true: fire once per character, ever.

directive.description: Narrator-visible for the one turn it fires. {name} is the character.

sets_flag.description: Flag set once the exit scene is narrated. {id} is the character's first name, lowercased (Lark Ferris -> lark). Declare each resulting flag in mechanics.flags.declared so a condition can read it.

directive.x-visible-when: one turn, when the rule fires

reduced_directive.x-visible-when: one turn, when the rule fires

engine_revelations.$comment: Fragments: information held back until a trigger happens on the page - backstory, a memory, lore, a secret, a clue. Not only memories: the narrator is shown revealed content under a neutral heading, so each entry's content says what it is. A revealed fragment is also a condition leaf ({"revealed": id}) for threads, acts and endings.

title.x-visible-when: shown wherever a condition names the fragment
title.$comment: Author-only name for the fragment, shown on the storyboard wherever a condition names it. The engine never reads it and it is never prompted.

engine_lore.$comment: CR-06 keyed lore. Written by the board at its final path (D1); read by the keyed_lore engine (backend/mechanics/lore.py).

engine_bonds.$comment: CR-11 NPC-to-NPC bonds. One-way scores: A->B and B->A are separate, so unrequited feeling is representable. Read by the scored_bonds engine (backend/mechanics/bonds.py); state lives at state.mechanics.bonds[from][to].

axis.description: What the two ends of a bond mean, e.g. hostile and devoted.

registers.description: The closed vocabulary of things one character does to or for another, each with the amount it moves the bond, e.g. covered_for_them: 8, betrayed_them: -15. The state-update pass may only name these.

tiers.description: Labels for score bands, highest first by convention. Labels only: the narrator sees a tier label, never a number. A narration key is refused until a measurement shows labels are not enough (CR-11 decision 2).

seed.description: Starting scores between authored characters. A pair with no seed opens at 0 on its first event.

max_generated_bonds.description: How many bonds involving a generated character are kept. Past this, the one closest to neutral is evicted. Bonds between authored characters are never evicted.

cap_per_window.description: The most one bond may move in either direction within a window of turns.

side_cast_slot.$comment: CR-11 (r5 A): one role in a side-thread recipe. kind defaults to character. A character slot draws from any / authored / generated / followed (the character a followed thread had in `slot`) / an authored character's name; it never binds a protected character. A location slot names a world.locations id; an item slot names an inventory tag.

cast.description: The recipe's roles, keyed by slot name (e.g. a, b, place). Conditions and may_move name slots, not people.

premise.description: The situation the generator writes an episode from. Narrator-facing through the generated premise, so it goes through the leak check.

may_move.description: The only values this episode's premise and end conditions may involve: bond:<slot>,<slot>, relationship:<slot>, stat:<axis>, item:<tag>, leverage:<kind>.

follows.$comment: CR-11 (r5 C) callback: this recipe follows a concluded side thread, at most once per thread. Local to recipes on purpose - not a condition leaf, so no ending can read a side thread's outcome. Outcomes: resolved (its end condition or detect hit), failed (its fails_when), expired (reached max_turns), finale (concluded when the story's finale began), abandoned (a player thread offered abandon_after_offers times without advancing, CR-12). recipe may be player_pursuit, the synthetic recipe every player-started thread uses.

engine_side_threads.$comment: CR-11 side threads: a separate track of short AI-written episodes, started and ended by state, never by the story's structure. Not subplots: no delivers, never counted toward act advancement. Written by the board at its final path (D1); the episodic_threads engine reads it..

max_active.description: How many side threads can run at once. Their own pool: a side thread never takes an authored thread's slot.

cooldown_turns.description: Turns to wait after one side thread starts before another may.

start_after_beats.description: The pacing-loop beats after which a side thread may start. Names from mechanics.pacing_loop.beats. Required in practice: there is no default (lint errors on an absent or empty list, and the engine will refuse it when built).

max_turns.description: Every side thread ends by this many turns after it starts; the engine closes it if nothing else does.

protected.description: Authored characters no side thread may cast: someone whose arc the story needs to keep for itself.

default_recipe.description: When nothing authored is eligible, fall back to the built-in recipe: the pair with the strongest bond among characters seen recently. On unless set to false.

player_threads.$comment: CR-12 player-started side threads: a pursuit the protagonist chose off the rails, confirmed in code by repeated reports, then run with every CR-11 guarantee (end conditions, detect, the max_turns backstop). Absent means the feature does not exist (P-2). Replaces the save's player_driven_goals once the engine is built.

max_active.description: How many player-started threads can run at once. Their own count: the engine's pool never blocks one.

confirm.description: A pursuit opens a thread only after being reported this many times within this many turns, so one curious scene never becomes a thread.

abandon_after_offers.description: A player thread offered this many times without advancing ends as abandoned: the player lost interest.

may_move.description: What a pursuit's premise and end conditions may involve. relationship:cast means the relationships of whoever the pursuit casts; otherwise relationship:<authored character>, stat:<axis>, item:<tag>, leverage:<kind>.

vignettes.$comment: CR-11 (r5 B): single scenes of texture, no thread and no generation call. Seeds are narrator-visible.

every.description: At least this many turns between vignettes.

kind.description: destination: an ending the story is steered toward (the storyboard's Destination ending). terminal: an ending reached through stats at any time, never steered toward (the storyboard's Failure ending). A catch-all is not a kind: it is a destination with no viable_while (the storyboard's Catch-all checkbox).

viable_while.$comment: The ending stays possible only while this holds; the moment it goes false the ending is pruned for good. Leave it off to make this destination the catch-all (at least one is required).

hint.x-visible-when: a pacing nudge, at most one per nudge

epilogue.x-visible-when: shown to the player after THE END

cast.$comment: The authored characters this thread involves (world.characters keys). Author-only for now: the storyboard uses it; no engine reads it yet, and it is never prompted.

story_clock.$comment: CR-13 (Story_Mechanics_Update.md): turns that move nothing don't spend the story's budget, up to a free streak. Absent means every turn counts. Read by the engine (backend/clock.py): the ending budget and its checks, the act-check cadence, turn_gte conditions and stat per_turn drift run on a second counter that idle turns past the free streak advance.

free_idle_streak.description: How many turns in a row that move nothing (a question, a look around) cost the story no time. After that the options lean forward, the push directive fires once, and idle turns count again.

push_directive.description: Narrator-facing, one turn, when the free streak is used up: something in the world that moves, in the story's own voice. Optional: without it only the options lean forward.
